title: Attila and the Huns
objective: After this level you can describe the Huns under Attila and their impact on the empire.
summary: Attila squeezed gold from the East, was stopped in Gaul in 451 CE and turned back from Italy in 452. His empire died with him in 453.

cards.headline: Christian writers called him the “Scourge of God.”
cards.body: Attila, king of the Huns, earned that name the hard way. Here’s how, and why his power didn’t outlive him.

cards.headline: King of the Huns
cards.body: Remember the Huns from Level 89, the steppe horsemen whose push west drove the Goths across the Danube? Attila ruled them from 434 to 453 CE, at first sharing power with his brother Bleda. He raided the Eastern Empire and forced it to pay him large amounts of gold. For once, the Romans were the ones handing over the treasure.

cards.headline: Stopped twice
cards.body: In 451 CE Attila invaded Gaul. A Roman and Visigothic army under the general Aetius stopped him at the Battle of the Catalaunian Plains. Yes, Visigoths: 41 years after sacking Rome, they fought on Rome’s side. In 452 CE Attila invaded Italy instead. Pope Leo I met him, and Attila withdrew. A general stopped him in Gaul; a pope met him in Italy.

cards.context: Attila died in 453 CE, and his empire of many peoples soon fell apart. It had depended on Attila himself to hold it together. Without him, the Scourge of God’s empire lasted about as long as a sandcastle at high tide.

questions.prompt: Who stopped Attila in Gaul in 451 CE?
questions.explanation: Aetius led a Roman and Visigothic army that stopped Attila at the Catalaunian Plains.

questions.prompt: Why did the Huns’ empire fall apart so quickly?

options.label: A plague killed all their horses

questions.explanation: Attila’s empire of many peoples fell apart soon after he died in 453 CE.
